title: New Materialism and Its Implications for Research in Social Science
abstract: ABSTRACT New Materialism is a philosophical framework that has gained some popularity in social science research in recent years, including in the systemic field. Despite its growing popularity and, arguably, its strong relevance to systemic and other social science researchers, there is no targeted guidance on how to implement this framework in research, particularly for early‐career researchers and students—a clear gap in the methodological literature. Therefore, we provide an overview of New Materialism as a philosophical tradition, offer a guide for researchers on using this approach, and present a case study that exemplifies its implementation in research. Students and early‐career academics unfamiliar with this framework are invited to consult this paper and related resources to help them implement New Materialism in their scholarly activities. We argue that researching social phenomena through the lens of New Materialism can enable researchers to reflect on structural issues, the interdependency and mutual influence between humans and non‐human aspects of modern life, and how multiple, complex narratives may co‐occur despite the desire to construct simple, linear answers in social research, all of high relevance to systemic thinkers.
